_README: Every leaf in this file MUST have a `value` and a non-empty `source`. The eval harness refuses to emit a reportable number while any `source` is empty. Fill these from published material before Sept 1 — a cited constraint is worth more to a reviewer than a confident guess.
_units: Probabilities are 0..1. Money is integer paise. Time is hours.

retry_success_by_attempt._note: P(a retry of a previously failed charge succeeds), indexed by attempt number.

1.source: Recurly (40M-transaction analysis, 2025): a Day1/3/5/7 retry schedule recovers ~58% of failed payments through retries alone. Chargebee's 2025 dunning benchmark: full automated dunning (retries + contact) recovers 70-80% cumulatively. Both confirm the MAGNITUDE this table's cumulative recovery lands in and the declining-by-attempt SHAPE; neither publishes a per-payment-method (card/UPI/e-mandate), per-attempt breakdown at this granularity, so the specific split below is this project's own reasoned interpolation, not independently verified attempt-by-attempt.

retry_timing_multiplier._note: Multiplier on retry_success_by_attempt as a function of hours waited since the failure. Captures salary-cycle and balance-replenishment effects.

lt_6h.source: Stripe 2025 Smart Retries documentation: retrying at an optimal time of day (vs. immediately) increases per-retry recovery by 10-15%. Confirms timing affects retry success directionally; Stripe's finding is about time-of-day, while this table's buckets are about elapsed hours since failure (salary-cycle effects) — a related but distinct phenomenon, so Stripe's 10-15% figure should not be read as validating this table's specific multiplier magnitudes.

failure_reason_recoverability._note: Multiplier by declared failure reason. A hard decline is not a soft decline; treating them alike is the single most common flaw in retry logic.

mandate_paused_by_customer._note: Governs the NUDGE branch only — a charge against a paused mandate is hard-blocked in response-model.frozen.js regardless of this number. A message can still prompt the customer to resume it themselves, since only they hold that switch.

mandate_paused_by_business._note: Deliberately zero for BOTH retry and nudge. The block is on the business side, so contacting the customer accomplishes nothing — the only correct action today is ESCALATE_HUMAN, because no intervention in the current set can call the API that would actually resume it. That gap is documented in README.md as a known limitation, not hidden by giving this a comforting non-zero number.

opt_out_hazard._note: P(customer opts out permanently) per contact. Opt-out is not a neutral outcome — it destroys all future recovery on that customer, so it is priced, not ignored.

payment_link_sms.source: SMS opt-out benchmarks, 2026 (DigitalApplied's 110-point aggregate; Twilio; Omnisend): per-send opt-out medians run ~0.42% overall, with finance/banking specifically at ~0.28% (the lowest-attrition vertical measured) and "good" programs universally under 1%. This project's 1.2% is deliberately set ABOVE the general marketing benchmark, reasoned (not measured) on the basis that a payment-recovery message is a debt reminder, not a marketing message, and debt reminders are understood in collections practice to provoke more opt-outs than promotional content — but no benchmark specific to payment-recovery messaging (as opposed to general marketing) was found.

payment_link_sms.source: India A2P SMS market rate, 2026: DLT-registered transactional SMS costs ~₹0.10-0.20 per message (Message Central, WebXion, MetaReach, MessageBot — cross-checked across four independent pricing pages, all converging on this range). 25 paise sits within this range, consistent with a mid-market provider plus minor markup.

payment_link_whatsapp.source: Meta WhatsApp Business Platform, India rates (Jan 2026 revision): utility-category templates (which a payment-status reminder qualifies as, per Meta's own category rules) cost ~₹0.145 per message at the platform level; BSPs typically add 15-35% markup (AiSensy, Blueticks, Monty Mobile, EngageLab). This project's cost was corrected from an earlier 80-paise placeholder (which priced this as a marketing-tier message) down to a utility-tier estimate with markup.

human_cost_per_hour_paise.source: India BPO/call-center agent cost, 2026, voice support, offshore-delivered: consistently $6-18/hour across seven independent industry sources (1840&Co, TheOctopusTech, GigaBPO, AB7 Solutions, CallForce, Mascallnet, Awaaz.ai — the last giving ₹8-20/minute-equivalent for a fully-loaded Tier-1/2 city BPO agent). This project's original 350₹/hr placeholder was below every source found; corrected to ₹700/hr, near the middle of the converged range.

opt_out_loss_paise._note: Expected forgone future recovery from one opted-out customer. Without this number an agent that spams everyone looks optimal.
